# Signet Jewelers + GrowthBook
Date: 2026-10-02 | Duration: 52.119998931884766m

## Summary
The discussion examined how legal and organizational caution slows official AI adoption at Signet, even as leadership supports it and teams use AI informally with human oversight. Signet also faces inefficiencies from rebuilding successful experiment variants for production, while AI could synthesize thousands of experiments, identify patterns, and improve feature design across brands. Analytics teams struggle with data overload and slow reporting. GrowthBook’s warehouse-native model was presented as a way to retain data ownership, avoid vendor lock-in, customize statistical analysis, and connect experiment results with a living learning library. Dynamic Yield remains enterprise-strong and benefits from Mastercard data, but Signet values smaller, faster-moving vendors. Craig described an aspiration for 80% personalization and 20% A/B testing, potentially supported by Contextual Bandits. Signet documents experiments through plans, newsletters, Confluence, and leadership reviews, but much of this process remains manual. GrowthBook’s automated reporting, learning aggregation, natural-language analytics, and product analytics features generated interest, despite Signet’s recent three-year Dynamic Yield renewal.

## Keywords
Dynamic Yield, AI agents, experimentation lifecycle, cross-banner learnings, personalization, data ownership

## Action Items

**Christian Liebenow**
Maintain close communication with Craig Kistler and provide updates on GrowthBook’s new and relevant data-centric features over the next six months to support Signet’s experimentation and AI initiatives (50:53)

**Graham McNicoll**
Share GrowthBook demo and related data-centric features with Signet teams as a follow-up to support their evaluation and potential adoption (24:50)

**Craig Kistler**
Keep GrowthBook on the procurement and vendor shortlist for potential RFP processes during the Dynamic Yield contract period, ensuring consideration for future experimentation and personalization solutions (49:40)
